pairs.question: Quare reversi estis?
pairs.answer: Vir occurrit nobis et dixit ad nos ite revertimini ad regem qui misit vos.
pairs.derivation: Ohozias asks the returning messengers why they came back. Answer is the messengers' reply; cut at the first sentence that answers the 'why' (a man met us and told us to go back), dropping the framing 'at illi responderunt ei' and stopping before the continued report 'et dicetis ei haec dicit Dominus...' which is the quoted oracle, not the reason for return.

pairs.question: Cuius figurae et habitu est vir qui occurrit vobis et locutus est verba haec?
pairs.answer: Vir pilosus et zona pellicia accinctis renibus.
pairs.derivation: The king asks the appearance of the man. Dropped the speech tags 'qui dixit eis' and 'at illi dixerunt'. Answer ends at the physical description; the following 'qui ait Helias Thesbites est' is a separate identifying clause, not part of the appearance-answer, so it is cut.

pairs.question: Quid habes in domo tua?
pairs.answer: Non habeo ancilla tua quicquam in domo mea nisi parum olei quo unguear.
pairs.derivation: Heliseus's operative question to the widow; the preceding framing 'cui dixit Heliseus quid vis ut faciam tibi dic mihi' is dropped, taking the actual interrogative 'quid habes in domo tua'. Answer drops the tag 'at illa respondit' and runs to the full stop.

pairs.question: Quid ergo vult ut faciam ei?
pairs.answer: Filium enim non habet et vir eius senex est.
pairs.derivation: Heliseus asks Giezi what can be done for the Shunammite. Dropped the tags 'et ait' and 'dixitque Giezi ne quaeras'; the answer 'filium enim non habet et vir eius senex est' (she has no son and her husband is old) directly supplies what is wanted.

pairs.question: Quare dominus meus flet?
pairs.answer: Quia scio quae facturus sis filiis Israhel mala.
pairs.derivation: Azahel asks why the man of God weeps; quare answered by quia. Dropped tags 'cui Azahel ait' and 'at ille respondit'. Cut at the sense-break before the elaborating list of evils 'civitates eorum munitas igne succendes...', keeping the direct cause.

pairs.question: Quid tibi dixit Heliseus?
pairs.derivation: Benadad asks Azahel what Heliseus said. Dropped tags 'qui ait ei' and 'at ille respondit'; answer reports what was said and runs to the end of the utterance.

pairs.question: Quinam estis vos?
pairs.answer: Fratres Ahaziae sumus et descendimus ad salutandos filios regis et filios reginae.
pairs.derivation: Hieu asks who they are. Dropped tags 'dixitque ad eos' and 'at illi responderunt'; the answer identifies them and their purpose, kept whole as one coherent reply.

pairs.question: Vis ut accedat umbra decem lineis an ut revertatur totidem gradibus?
pairs.answer: Facile est umbram crescere decem lineis nec hoc volo ut fiat sed ut revertatur retrorsum decem gradibus.
pairs.derivation: Esaias poses an alternative question (vis... an...) about the sign; framing 'cui ait Esaias hoc erit signum a Domino quod facturus sit Dominus sermonem quem locutus est' is dropped as setup-narration, keeping the interrogative. Ezechias's reply (tag 'et ait Ezechias' dropped) chooses the second option and is kept whole.

pairs.question: Quid dixerunt viri isti aut unde venerunt ad te?
pairs.answer: De terra longinqua venerunt de Babylone.
pairs.derivation: Esaias asks what the men said and whence they came. Dropped framing 'venit autem Esaias propheta ad regem Ezechiam dixitque ei' and the answer-tag 'cui ait Ezechias'; the reply answers the 'whence' part and runs to the full stop.

pairs.question: Quid viderunt in domo tua?
pairs.answer: Omnia quae sunt in domo mea viderunt.
pairs.derivation: Esaias asks what they saw. Dropped tags 'at ille respondit' and 'ait Ezechias'; cut at the first full stop before the elaboration 'nihil est quod non monstraverim eis in thesauris meis', keeping the direct answer.
